newsitem.title: LEBANON: SOLIDERE shares mixed on week in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: SOLIDERE shares mixed on week in Beirut.

text.p: SOLIDERE shares were mixed in low turnover in the week ended on Friday but dealers said they expected prices to rise next week amid expectation that the company will issue GDRs worth $150 million.
"There is serious talk on the market about the GDR issue and this will have a positive effect on foreign investors," a dealer said.
A shares rose to $113.5 from last Friday's $111.25 and B shares fell to $113 from $115.
A shares rose steadily from $110 on Monday while B shares fluctuated, rising to a high of $113.625 on Wednesday, falling to $112.25 a day later but ending the week at $113.
Dealers said prices were erratic due to low volume as investors awaited the expected GDR (Global Depository Receipts) issue.
However, a big buy order on Friday which pushed up the price of B shares appeared to indicate the start of a more positive trend for next week, dealers said.
SOLIDERE has declined comment on the GDR reports but market sources say the issue is expected in mid-October.
The week's turnover in SOLIDERE shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange was 24,765 shares, compared with 25,291 a week earlier and value was $2,314,237.625 from $2,449,315.
Other shares traded during the week were 3,000 Ciments Libanais at $1.3125 and 1,000 Eternit at $1.875. There was also a block trade in 59,162 Ciments Libanais at $1.27.
There was no trade in the other listed companies Ciments Blancs and Uniceramic.
The Lebanon Invest Share Price Index (LISPI) rose 0.04 percent on the week to 84.04 and the BLOM Stock Index (BSI) rose 0.04 to 966.53.
